brief.headline: Georgianne was admitted after an Oct 31 ED visit for chest pain (cardiac workup negative). She has also been withdrawn, with 6 of 8 day center days missed and low mood after a friend's death, about 6 weeks after sertraline was started for a PHQ-9 of 14.

items.statement: On 2026-11-06 the day center reported 6 of the last 8 scheduled days missed. When present she was quiet and left activities early. On 2026-11-08 she told the social worker she feels "down" and does not want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. Depression screening and grief support were planned.
items.verifier_note: Both notes match the statement. The dates, the 6 of 8 missed days, the quiet behavior and early departures, the "down" mood, the friend's death last month, and the planned depression screening and grief support are all present.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-25 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), with a recheck planned in 4 weeks. The pharmacist added it to the blister pack on 2026-09-27. The notes show no documented 4-week recheck or repeat PHQ-9. Withdrawal and low mood were reported in November.
items.verifier_note: The start date, dose, PHQ-9 of 14, 4-week recheck plan, and pharmacist blister-pack update are all supported. The cited notes show no recheck or repeat PHQ-9. "Withdrawal" is not stated in the notes. They describe missed day center days, being quiet, and not wanting to leave the house, so "withdrawal" is an interpretation and could be misread as medication withdrawal.

items.statement: She was seen in the partner hospital ED on 2026-10-31 for chest pain and admitted for 3 days. Cardiac workup was negative and no new medications were started at discharge. The PCP follow-up on 2026-11-06 found her back to baseline per her grandson, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The discharge summary and the PCP note support the 10-31 ED visit for chest pain, the 3-day admission, the negative cardiac workup, and no new medications. They also support the 11-06 follow-up (back to baseline per her grandson) and the plan to monitor closely for two weeks.

items.statement: On 2026-11-26 she attended day center, joined chair exercise and the music group, and ate most of lunch. This is a possible improvement in engagement after the missed days.
items.verifier_note: The 11-26 note documents attendance, chair exercise, music group, and eating most of lunch. Calling it a possible improvement is a hedged interpretation.

items.statement: There is no influenza vaccine on record this season (season start 2026-08-01). The last flu vaccine was 2026-02-13.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season (season start 2026-08-01). The last influenza vaccine was 2026-02-13.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review date is captured so changes are compared against the correct baseline.

Medication changes: verify sertraline 25 mg start on 2026-09-25 against the prescriber order, indication (PHQ-9 of 14), dose, and any titration or follow-up plan; check for any other starts or stops in the window, including the long-standing vitamin B12 injection (last administration date and whether the schedule is still current).

Mood and depression follow-up: repeat PHQ-9 or equivalent since sertraline start, review any suicidality screening documentation, note therapy or counseling referrals, and check for sleep, appetite, and energy changes reported by the participant or caregiver.

Early sertraline tolerability: look for documented adverse effects (GI upset, sleep change, agitation, dizziness, falls, bleeding or bruising) and whether the prescriber has scheduled a response check.

Falls, ED visits, and admissions in the window: review incident reports, ED or hospital notifications, and any unplanned visits, and note whether any relate to dizziness or balance given the new medication.
Weight trend: compare weights across the window, since prediabetes and a new antidepressant both make appetite and weight change relevant; flag change of more than 5% or a steady trend.
Blood pressure and vitals: review readings in the window and flag any abnormal or trending values for clinician review.
Glycemic monitoring for prediabetes: check the most recent A1c or fasting glucose, date of last lab, and whether repeat testing or lifestyle/diabetes-prevention program referral is due.
Function and ADLs: compare current ADL and IADL status (bathing, dressing, medications, transport, meals) with the prior review, and check for any new assistance needs.
Cognition: check for any screening (e.g., MoCA or Mini-Cog) or observed changes since the last review, and note whether depressive symptoms could be confounding cognitive findings.

Attendance, caregiver, and care-plan items: review PACE center attendance and any missed days, caregiver or social situation changes, and care-plan goals or assessments due in or before 2026-11-30. Note that allergies are recorded as none and verify this is current.
